plan.title: docs(agents): surface Windows %APPDATA%\\deft\\USER.md in always-on session bootstrap

narratives.Description: Always-on AGENTS session routing omits the Windows USER.md path, so agents invent ~/.config/deft and report USER.md missing. This story surfaces the platform default (and a resolve-verb mandate) without changing the onboarding write location.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

Session bootstrap tells agents to read `USER.md` and confirm alignment, but the always-on surface (`AGENTS.md` / managed Session routing) does **not** name the platform path. Agents then guess Unix XDG (`~/.config/deft/USER.md` / `C:\Users\<user>\.config\deft\USER.md`) and report USER.md missing on native Windows even when the file is present at the correct location.

## Evidence (this session)

1. Agent searched `./USER.md` and `C:\Users\msada\.config\deft\USER.md` — both missing.
2. Operator pointed at the real file: `C:\Users\msada\AppData\Roaming\deft\USER.md` (`%APPDATA%\deft\USER.md`).
3. That is exactly where setup / Platform Detection put it (`content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md`, `resolveUserMdPath` rung 3).
4. Runtime resolution is fine (`packages/core/src/user-config/resolve-user-md.ts`); the gap is **agent discovery**, not the resolver.

## Why this bites

- `#2271` fixed programmatic first-hit-wins resolution for CLI/session-start code paths.
- Interactive agents still follow prose: "read USER.md" without a path table, so they invent `~/.config/deft` on Windows.
- Alignment confirmation then fails or skips Personal (always wins) addressing-name until the human corrects the path.

## Expected

Always-on or near-always-on guidance (AGENTS.md Session routing / session-start ritual / a one-line `task` diagnostic) should make the platform default unmistakable:

| Platform | Default USER.md |
|---|---|
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\deft\USER.md` |
| Unix | `~/.config/deft/USER.md` |
| Override | `$DEFT_USER_PATH` |
| Workspace bridge | `<project>/.deft/USER.md` |

Concrete options (pick one or combine):

1. **Pointer in managed Session routing** — one compact line: resolve via `task session:start` / shared order; on win32 prefer `%APPDATA%\deft`, not `~/.config`.
2. **Agent-facing resolve verb** — e.g. `task user:show-path` / session-start already prints `USER.md resolved (platform-config): …` — mandate agents use that output instead of filesystem guessing.
3. **⊗ anti-pattern** — do not treat `~\.config\deft` as canonical on Windows.

## Non-goals

- Changing the Windows onboarding write location (Roaming is correct).
- Replacing `#2271` search order.

## Acceptance

- A fresh Windows interactive session finds `%APPDATA%\deft\USER.md` without the operator supplying the path.
- Agents no longer conclude "USER.md missing" solely because `~\.config\deft` is absent on win32.

## Related

- #2271 / PR #2290 (resolver search order — code path OK)
- Setup skill already documents the table; always-on AGENTS path does not
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows maintainer, I want always-on session bootstrap to name %APPDATA%\deft\USER.md, so that agents find Personal preferences without guessing XDG paths.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update the managed Session routing pointer in content/templates/agents-entry.md (and refresh AGENTS.md) so win32 agents are told to read %APPDATA%\\deft\\USER.md rather than inventing ~/.config/deft.
2. Add a content/unit contract or packages/core/src/user-config test that asserts the documented resolve order and fails if the Windows AppData path disappears from always-on bootstrap text.
3. Verify with task agents:refresh plus the focused user-config test module so evidence shows agents can locate USER.md without operator paste.
narratives.Acceptance:
1. Always-on bootstrap names Windows AppData USER.md
2. Resolver path remains authoritative
3. Regression test guards the pointer

items.title: Always-on bootstrap names Windows AppData USER.md

narrative.Acceptance: Given a native Windows session bootstrap, when an agent reads the managed Session routing card, then it shows %APPDATA%\\deft\\USER.md as the default path and rejects inventing ~/.config/deft.
Given DEFT_USER_PATH is unset, when resolveUserMdPath runs on win32, then it returns the Roaming AppData deft USER.md path and the bootstrap prose matches that order.
Given the content contract or user-config test suite, when the Windows path pointer is removed, then the focused test fails before merge.
